question.text: How many miles driven autonomously will Tesla Robotaxi have driven as of December 1, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as Tesla's live estimate for millions of autonomous miles driven by its Robotaxi, as presented by [Robotaxi Stats](https://www.robotaxistats.com/) on its latest snapshot timestamped on December 1, 2026 (PST) (i.e., before midnight on December 2, 2026).
question.fine_print:
In case of any issues with the main resolution source not presenting a snapshot for that date, Metaculus may check the main [Tesla page](https://www.tesla.com/robotaxi) and resolve based on the number presented there. 

Other credible sources may also be used.

research:
I couldn't find any source that settles this yet. The latest snapshot shows 4.81M miles, below the question's 5.0M floor, and it will pass that floor in a few days. The counter looks like a straight-line projection of about 80,000 miles a day from Tesla's last report. If it stays on that line, it reaches about 6.6-6.7M by the end of Dec 1 (my calculation). A new Tesla report could raise the rate.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-09 (about 03:20 PT): Robotaxi Stats shows "Tesla's live estimate" at **4.81M driverless miles** (counter 4,806,465). The site labels this an estimate, not a measured total. This is the most recent snapshot I could reach. [robotaxistats](https://www.robotaxistats.com/)
- The same page shows the confirmed figure: 3.1M miles through 2026-10-18, from Tesla's Robotaxi Safety Report, covering Jan 22 to Oct 18. By city: Austin 2.12M, Dallas 608K, Houston 226K, Orlando 61K, Tampa 53K, Miami 46K. [robotaxistats](https://www.robotaxistats.com/)
- tesla.com/robotaxi returned HTTP 403, so I could not check the fallback source.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet.
- The counter readings fit a fixed-rate projection: 3.1M on Oct 18, past 3.3M on Oct 21, about 4.0-4.1M on Oct 30-31, and 4.81M on Nov 9. That works out to roughly 78-81K miles a day. It matches the "80,600 miles/day" figure Sawyer Merritt posted on 2026-10-21. My inference is that the counter projects forward from the last report at a fixed pace and resets when Tesla publishes new data. [basenor](https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/tesla-robotaxi-hits-80-600-miles-per-day-launches-first-responder-training-site), [notateslaapp](https://notateslaapp.com/news/4860/tesla-names-next-robotaxi-cities-shares-miles-driven-safety-data)
- My projection: 4.806M + about 22.9 days × 80.6K ≈ **6.65M** at the end of Dec 1 PST, if the rate doesn't change.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-11: TSLA rose 1.8% after Tesla extended its Austin geofence on Nov 9. [247wallst](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/11/how-much-is-teslas-robotaxi-actually-worth/)
- 2026-11-10: A reviewer reports the Cybercab is running in Austin, with a Dallas rollout planned for late November. [T3](https://www.t3.com/auto/i-rode-in-cybercab-and-now-think-waymos-days-could-be-numbered-why-teslas-latest-marks-the-end-of-cybertruck-poses-questions-to-uber)
- 2026-11-09: Tesla launched in San Antonio with a zone of about 275 sq mi, its 8th city. Jacksonville, Las Vegas and Phoenix are listed as "coming soon." [Statesman](https://www.statesman.com/business/article/tesla-robotaxi-san-antonio-launch-austin-expansion-22520721.php), [Mashable](https://mashable.com/tech/tesla-robotaxi-san-antonio)
- 2026-10-31: NextBigFuture claims about 700K unsupervised miles a week, up from 558K in the week of Oct 12-18, with 17-20% weekly growth. It projects about 2M miles a week by late November and says 300 Cybercabs each are planned for Dallas and Houston in November. It also cites 4.0-4.1M cumulative on Oct 30-31. These are blogger estimates. [NBF](https://www.nextbigfuture.com/2026/10/tesla-robotaxi-ramp-in-texas-and-florida-tracking-to-pass-waymo-by-end-of-2026.html)
- 2026-10-27: Electrek reports Tesla's best week at 558K miles, of which Austin was 438K (up 30% week over week), Dallas 95K, and the four smaller markets about 25K combined. Waymo drives about 7x more. [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/10/27/musk-robotaxi-victory-waymo-austin-miles/)
- 2026-10-21: Tesla published its first Robotaxi Safety Report: 3.11M miles through Oct 18. [driveteslacanada](https://driveteslacanada.ca/?p=126145)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- Cumulative driverless miles over time:
  - Late July (Q2 report): about 0.38M
  - 2026-09-03: 1.0M. About 620K of that came in the prior six weeks, roughly 15K a day. [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/09/03/tesla-announces-1-million-unsupervised-miles-driven-by-robotaxi/)
  - 2026-10-18: 3.1M, about 45K a day since Sep 3, with the latest week at about 80K a day.
  - 2026-11-09: 4.81M on the counter.
- Actual weekly miles have grown fast, roughly 20-30% a week in October.
- Implied range for Dec 1 (my calculation):
  - Flat counter rate: about 6.6-6.7M.
  - If actual miles grew about 15% a week from 100K a day in early November: roughly 7.5-8.5M, but the counter only shows this if Tesla publishes updated data that resets it.
- This is not seasonal. The series is too new to have earlier years for comparison.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market on robotaxi miles.
- Related Kalshi markets for Tesla robotaxi states offered in 2026: Florida 0.90, Nevada 0.62, Arizona 0.47.
- Polymarket puts a California launch by Dec 31 at 0.03.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- A second Safety Report. I couldn't find its schedule. If it is monthly, Tesla could publish around Nov 18-25 with data through about Nov 15. That would probably raise the counter's rate given the weekly growth.
- Cybercab rollout in Dallas in late November, plus about 300 vehicles each planned for Dallas and Houston.
- Ramp-up in San Antonio and the expanded Austin geofence, and possible launches in Jacksonville, Las Vegas and Phoenix.
- Holiday travel around Thanksgiving (Nov 26).
- Risk: if Robotaxi Stats has no Dec 1 snapshot, resolution falls back to tesla.com, which blocked automated access.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-09, about 3:20 AM PT: Robotaxi Stats shows "Tesla's live estimate" at **4.81M (4,806,465)** driverless miles. The site describes Tesla's counter as an "estimate at fleet's current pace". It also shows Tesla's confirmed figure of 3.1M through Oct 18, as a range of "3.1M-4.81M". The page header says "as of Nov 10 PT" and the footer says "Data updated Nov 8, 11:05 PM PT", so the site does not refresh the counter often. [robotaxistats](https://www.robotaxistats.com/)
- The site has no archive of past counter readings. tracker.json holds only the Nov 9 reading, and the changelog's only Tesla mileage entry is the Oct 21 safety report showing 3.1M. The methodology page does not say how often the counter is read. [tracker.json](https://www.robotaxistats.com/data/tracker.json), [changelog](https://www.robotaxistats.com/changelog/), [methodology](https://www.robotaxistats.com/methodology/)
- Confirmed miles by city through Oct 18: Austin 2.118M, Dallas 0.608M, Houston 0.226M, Orlando 61K, Tampa 53K, Miami 46K. These add up to about 3.11M. [robotaxistats](https://www.robotaxistats.com/)
- I could not read tesla.com/robotaxi or tesla.com/robotaxi/safety, which is the fallback source; both returned HTTP 403.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet.
- If Robotaxi Stats publishes no new counter reading by Dec 1, the stale 4.81M figure could in theory be what decides it. That is below the question's range.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)

It projects about 2M miles per week by the last week of November, with roughly 600 more Cybercabs in Dallas and Houston. [selfdrivenews](https://selfdrivenews.com/tesla-robotaxi-safety-report-driverless-miles/), [tao.media](https://www.tao.media/tesla-publishes-robotaxi-safety-data-for-3-3-million-driverless-miles/)

### 4. Base rates and trend
How cumulative unsupervised miles have grown:
- About 2026-07-22 (Q2 call): about 0.38M. [NotATeslaApp](https://www.notateslaapp.com/news/4486/tesla-robotaxi-hits-380k-unsupervised-miles-names-next-markets)
- 2026-09-03: 1M, about 15K per day since July. [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/09/03/tesla-announces-1-million-unsupervised-miles-driven-by-robotaxi/)
- 2026-09-30: nearly 2M, about 37K per day. [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/business/37705)
- 2026-10-18: 3.1M, about 61K per day.
- About 2026-10-31: about 4.1M (blog figure), about 77K per day.
- 2026-11-09: 4.81M (live estimate), about 78K per day over 22 days.

My extrapolation over the 22 days from Nov 9 to Dec 1:
- At a flat 78K per day: about 6.5M.
- At 100K per day: about 7.0M.
- With weekly miles growing about 15 to 20% a week: about 7.3 to 7.6M.
- On NBF's aggressive path, 2M miles per week by late November: around 8 to 9M.

Two caveats:
- The counter is Tesla's own extrapolation, so it may move in steps when Tesla re-bases it.
- The series is only about 4 months old, so there is no seasonal history. A Thanksgiving dip in late November is possible.

### 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on Robotaxi miles.
- Related markets:
  - Kalshi, robotaxi offered in a state by end of 2026: Florida 0.90, Nevada 0.62, Arizona 0.47.
  - Polymarket, Tesla robotaxi in California by Dec 31: 0.03.
- NextBigFuture is the only expert-style projection I found, and it is bullish (see section 3).

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late November: the Cybercab rollout in Dallas, and possibly about 300 Cybercabs each for Dallas and Houston, per NBF.
- The new San Antonio service and the larger Austin geofence should add miles.
- Possible launches in Las Vegas, Phoenix or Jacksonville.
- Tesla may publish a safety report update that re-bases the counter.
- How often Robotaxi Stats refreshes is a key risk: a stale reading would make the number lower.
- Tesla's Q4 earnings come in late January, after resolution.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** About 20 days. Resolution uses the last Robotaxi Stats snapshot timestamped December 1, 2026 (PST).

(b) **Latest known value:** 4.81M miles (counter 4,806,465) on Robotaxi Stats, around 03:20 PT on 2026-11-09. The confirmed figure is 3.1M miles through Oct 18, from Tesla's Safety Report.

(c) **If nothing changed:** The counter is a fixed-rate projection of about 80.6K miles a day from Tesla's last report. Left as is, it reaches about 6.6-6.65M by late Dec 1 PST. The exact figure depends on when in the day the snapshot is taken. A frozen counter at about 4.8M is very unlikely.

(d) **If the trend continued:**
- With no new report, the counter is about 6.65M.
- Actual weekly miles grew 10-20% a week in October. If Tesla publishes a new report around mid-to-late November, the counter would reset to a higher base and a faster rate. That gives roughly 7.5-8.5M by Dec 1, assuming growth continued.
- If growth stalled, a reset would leave the figure near 6.6M, or even slightly below it.

(e) **Historical variation:**
- Cumulative miles went from 1.0M (Sep 3) to 3.1M (Oct 18) to 4.8M (Nov 9, projected).
- Over a 3-week window, the counter moves about 1.7-1.85M at the current rate.
- Real growth has been fast, with weekly miles up 20-30% in October.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- No market exists on this quantity.
- NextBigFuture, a blogger, projects about 2M miles a week by late November, which would be well above the counter.
- The question creator's range is 5-15M.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- *Low:* A Tesla update that reveals slower actual miles, or a safety incident or pause. Either would reset the counter lower or slow its rate, for about 6.0M.
- *High:* A report showing 1M+ miles a week, with the Cybercab fleet in Dallas and Houston and the San Antonio and Austin expansions. The reset rate could then exceed 150K a day, for about 9-10M.
